title: Discrepancy Theory: An Algorithmic and Geometric Perspective
summary: Combinatorial discrepancy theory is a subject with roots in combinatorics, geometry, and number theory, and with numerous applications to mathematics and computer science. At its core, discrepancy theory is about dividing a collection of objects into two parts that are as balanced as possible. For example, given a collection of subsets of a finite universe, we may wish to color the elements with two colors so that each set is approximately evenly split.
